comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Historical description-size calibration (2026-08-10) — operator-directed blocking limit

Method: replayed CREATE/EDIT history, including retired events, for every bug/story/task/epic in the tracker. For each plan-review and completion-verifier sidecar, reconstructed the authoritative description length at that event timestamp. Corpus: 2,202 work tickets, 4,037 plan-review events, and 1,121 completion-verifier events. This avoids using only current text after later edits.

Distribution across work tickets: p50 1,844 chars; p75 3,031; p90 4,477; p95 5,331; p97.5 6,337; p99 7,500; maximum 15,853. The current 24,000-character cap is above the historical maximum and therefore cannot protect either gate.

Candidate 8,000-character cutoff: 18/2,202 current work tickets (0.82%) meet or exceed it. Plan review at >=8,000 chars: 41 events across 8 tickets, median 553.7s and p90 981.9s, versus 389.5s/p90 711.2s below the cutoff. Completion verification at >=8,000 chars: 14 events with 50.0% PASS, versus 74.3% below; first-attempt PASS was 57.1% across 7 tickets, versus 73.7% below. At >=10,000 the signal is stronger but the sample shrinks to two reviewed tickets and would miss the 8–10K pain range. At 6,000 the signal exists but would block 3.18% of work tickets, which is unnecessarily broad.

Decision: set the default maximum description length to 8,000 characters and make exceeding it BLOCKING. This is a generous tail limit just above p99, not a normal-writing target. It should apply before both plan review and completion verification so an oversized ticket is decomposed before consuming a gate run. Keep the value config-driven. The ticket description's prior requirements that P4 remain advisory/never block are superseded by this operator decision and must be revised before implementation.

Limits: description length correlates with ticket complexity, so the history does not prove length alone causes every failure. The cutoff is justified operationally: it touches <1% of tickets while capturing the range with materially worse wall time and completion reliability.

compiled_state.description:
## Context

Large ticket descriptions materially degrade both plan review and completion verification. The existing P4 description signal is advisory at 24,000 characters, above the historical maximum, so it cannot protect either gate.

Historical replay is complete and recorded in the ticket comments. The corpus covered 2,202 work tickets, 4,037 plan-review events, and 1,121 completion-verifier events. Current descriptions were p99 7,500 characters and maximum 15,853. At 8,000 characters, only 18/2,202 tickets (0.82%) were affected, while plan-review latency was materially worse and completion PASS rates were lower. The operator selected 8,000 as a generous blocking maximum.

This decision supersedes the old requirement that P4 never block. Other P4 signals remain advisory. This ticket does not add fuzzy severity labels, vacuity heuristics, or a second oversize criterion.

## Plan

- Add a typed [verify] maximum-description setting with a default of 8,000 characters. Exactly 8,000 characters is allowed; 8,001 blocks. Document the setting and require a positive integer.
- Keep description sizing in p4_oversize. A description above the configured maximum makes the P4 result blocking; AC-count and file-impact signals remain advisory and continue accumulating into the same P4 finding.
- In the light bug-review arm of workflow_ops.plan_review_precheck, partition DET blocks: retain only a blocking P4 description finding in det_blocking and downgrade every other DET block to advisory as before. Let that retained finding flow into the shared deterministic short circuit so an oversized light-tier bug returns BLOCK with coverage.llm_ran=false. Non-bug and blast-radius-escalated bug paths continue using the shared short circuit directly.
- In completion verification, check the authoritative ticket description after loading the same [verify] setting and before child checks or context assembly. Return the existing validated deterministic FAIL shape with an actionable split/shorten finding and make zero runner calls.
- Do not truncate, summarize, or elide ticket content. A ticket must be reduced below the maximum before either gate runs; force remains the operator escape hatch already provided by lifecycle commands.
- Add focused boundary, configuration, bug-tier, no-LLM-call, and advisory-regression tests. Keep the historical completion-recovery tests intact because they exercise the lower-level full-context recovery mechanism, not admission of a newly oversized ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The default maximum description length is 8,000 characters and is configurable through typed [verify] configuration.
- [ ] A description of exactly 8,000 characters is admitted and a description of 8,001 characters is blocked.
- [ ] Plan review returns a deterministic BLOCK with coverage.llm_ran=false before any LLM call when a work ticket exceeds the maximum.
- [ ] The blocking plan-review behavior applies to bug, story, task, and epic tickets; light bug review retains the P4 description block while downgrading other DET blocks.
- [ ] Completion verification returns a validated deterministic FAIL with zero runner calls when the authoritative ticket description exceeds the maximum.
- [ ] AC-count and file-impact P4 signals remain advisory when the description is within the maximum.
- [ ] P4 still emits at most one oversize finding, including when several size signals are present.
- [ ] Neither gate truncates, summarizes, or elides ticket content to get under the maximum.
- [ ] Documentation explains the default, the strict greater-than boundary, the historical calibration, and the existing force override.
- [ ] Focused tests, lint, typecheck, and the non-integration/non-external suite pass.
